title: Maximum Bitwise XOR After Rearrangement
summary: Given two binary strings s and t , each of length n , you are allowed to rearrange the characters in t in any order while keeping s unchanged.
statement: Given two binary strings s and t , each of length n , you are allowed to rearrange the characters in t in any order while keeping s unchanged. Return a binary string of length n that represents the maximum possible bitwise XOR value obtained by performing the bitwise XOR operation between s and the rearranged t .
constraints: s and t are nonempty binary strings of equal length.
You may rearrange t arbitrarily but may not rearrange s.
Return the lexicographically largest XOR string, which is also the largest binary value.
hints: A one at the earliest possible position dominates every later XOR bit.
Count zeroes and ones in t; for each bit of s, consume the opposite bit whenever available.
If the opposite supply is empty, consume the matching bit and append zero.
The exchange argument fixes the earliest bit optimally without harming any earlier choice, so repeating it yields the lexicographic maximum.
editorial: The exchange argument fixes the earliest bit optimally without harming any earlier choice, so repeating it yields the lexicographic maximum.

tests.explanation: Use rearrangement 110: XOR with 101 gives 011? A better rearrangement 011 gives 110, which is maximal.
